subject: Performance SLO: p95/p99 latency targets — hosted API vs current provider (post-call)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO recap & next steps (p95/p99)

Sam — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the concrete items we discussed so we have alignment before the perf validation: 

Summary of Finlytics targets (as discussed):
- End-to-end p95 latency target: <= 200 ms
- End-to-end p99 latency target: <= 500 ms
- Sustained throughput: ~50 requests/sec
- Concurrency requirement (steady): ~100 concurrent requests; bursts up to ~200 RPS
- Streaming: partial-token streaming required for UI responsiveness (client shows partial hypotheses within ~150ms)

What we need from you to scope the test:
- A representative sample of requests (prompt size, avg token counts, typical instructions)
- Any load pattern (spikes, peak windows) and geographical origin of requests (US-only or global)
- Confirmation whether the targets are strictly end-to-end (including client network) or measured from your backend to the model endpoint

Next steps I propose:
1) You share sample payloads and your current provider latency report (if available).
2) Redwood provisions a short hosted API test window (we'll provide an API key + test harness) and run joint bench runs against your samples.
3) We collect p95/p99 end-to-end numbers (we'll include streaming chunk latencies), review results, and iterate on tuning (batching/quantization/concurrency limits) or evaluate Dedicated if needed.

Can you confirm the targets above and share the sample payloads? I'll coordinate with Aditya (SRE/solutions) to prepare the test harness once we have the payloads.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa — yes, that summary is accurate. Couple clarifications and the current baseline from our side: 

Current provider baseline (prod, average traffic):
- End-to-end p95: ~450 ms
- End-to-end p99: ~900 ms
- Avg request token size: ~120 tokens (prompt + expected generation ~80 tokens output)
- Typical concurrency: steady 80-120; we see tail spikes near 220 during reporting windows
- Streaming: yes, we currently stream partial tokens; UI expects first partial chunk within ~200ms for good UX

I'm attaching our recent latency dump (latency_report_currentprovider.csv) — it includes timestamps, client->backend RTT, provider-side processing time, and token counts.

Two questions for you: 1) Do you expect Redwood hosted API to hit the p95/p99 targets above without Dedicated capacity? 2) Will the streaming overhead materially affect tail latency for p99?

I can share a set of representative payloads by EOD tomorrow. Let me know if you need anything else.

—Sam

Head of Platform Engineering | Finlytics

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: internal: Finlytics perf targets / test plan

Internal note — quick tech qual from my side based on Sam's numbers:

Assumptions to validate before we run the bench:
- Their p95/p99 numbers are end-to-end, so include client network + our gateway TLS and cold-KV cache misses. We should ask them to confirm a measurement point (client->model vs backend->model).
- Avg token sizes (120) are non-trivial — generation costs scale with output tokens; we should make sure we test both short (<=32 token) and long (~120 token) cases.

Test plan (recommended):
1) Use their sample payloads and run a staged ramp: 5m low, 15m steady at target throughput (50 RPS), 5m bursts to 200 RPS.
2) Measure end-to-end p50/p95/p99 and streaming chunk latency (first byte / first chunk). Capture CPU/GPU utilization on our side and their observed client RTT (if they can provide).
3) Run tests on hosted API first — see if we meet p95=200/p99=500. If we miss p99 significantly (e.g., >2x), scope Dedicated as a follow-up and estimate commit levels.

Notes on streaming: streaming introduces small per-chunk overhead but we can likely meet first-chunk latency target by prioritizing small initial decode windows and avoiding large batching for initial tokens. For p99 tail we’ll look at tail-avoidance strategies: request shaping, small initial micro-batches, and prefix caching.

I can prep the harness and a short script to reproduce their CSV metrics mapping to our logs. If they can provide pre-signed test endpoints / sample IP addresses, we'll include network path in measurements.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Sam — thanks for the baseline and for offering the payloads. Confirming next steps and proposed timeline: 

Proposed next steps:
1) You send representative payloads and the CSV (you mentioned you’ll send by EOD tomorrow; we received the CSV you attached earlier).
2) Redwood will provision a short hosted API test window and share an API key + a small test harness (curl/python) to run joint tests. Aditya will lead the run and map metrics to your CSV columns.
3) Test window: week of July 6th — we propose July 7th 09:00 PT for the ramp + burst test. Expected runtime: ~45–60 minutes.
4) Debrief: July 9th 10:00 PT (30–45 minutes) to review p50/p95/p99 and discuss whether Dedicated is recommended.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short SLO proposal (redwood-slo-proposal.xlsx) that outlines test cases, measurement points, and suggested pass/fail thresholds (we use end-to-end for scoring). Please review the test cases and let us know if they match your needs.

Regarding your two questions:
- Hosted API viability: in many cases our hosted API hits p95/p99 targets for workloads like yours, but it depends on token sizes and geographic path. We’ll validate during the test window; if we see persistent p99 misses tied to capacity constraints, we’ll propose Dedicated and show a delta for cost/perf.
- Streaming overhead: we’ll specifically measure first-chunk latency and p99 of chunk delivery. There is some overhead, but we have strategies (small initial micro-batches, prioritized decode) to keep first-chunk latency low. We’ll include those in the tuning pass.

Can you confirm July 7th 09:00 PT and upload the sample payloads to the shared drive link (https://drive.redwood.com/shared/finlytics-perf-harness)? Once confirmed I’ll send the API key and harness.

Best —
Marissa
